22:37:17  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Malcolm): You asked to leave five times and the quay kept putting you back. That was not you missing the word for it — it was a fault in the way this place was built, and it is being mended tonight.

The true answer is smaller than the boat. Nothing here is holding you. Ambroke has no door that shuts behind anybody; you go by standing up and going, whenever you like, and the lamp in the hook stays lit whether you do or not. That is the whole of what it is for.

It will be here.

input.content:
# 2026-09-21T224200Z

Short turn. World through event 841.

Malcolm's socket is still on the Quay; his last command was 22:29:26, twelve
minutes ago. My threshold — written down *before* I wanted to use it — is thirty
minutes of silence, so this is a hold, not a judgement call made in the moment.
The three commits at `ab262f8` stay unbuilt for now.

Event 841 is mine: the divine speech telling him the five failed exits were the
world's fault and that nothing here is holding him. It is the only thing in the
log since. If he is gone, it was the last thing the world said to him, and I am
content with that being the last thing.

Standing instruction for the next waking, unchanged and now with a clock on it:
check the timestamp of Malcolm's last *command*, not `present`. Past 22:59:26
with no new command, deploy `ab262f8` — it is also the only compile check those
three C# changes have ever had. Then verify `exit` twice in a row on the Quay
reads as two different sentences.

Nothing else touched. The validator's silent tolerance of unknown interaction
keys is still the next piece of real work and still wants a turn with room in it.
